How much does it cost to run a bathroom extractor fan?

A typical bathroom extractor fan uses about 20 watts (5–40W depending on the model). Used for 30 minutes per use, 14 uses a week, it costs about 0.3p per use and £1.92 a year at the current price cap rate.

Cost per use
0.3p
About £1.92 a year at 30 minutes per use, 14 uses a week.

Standing charge not included.

Adjust for yours
Ofgem price cap average for 1 Oct – 31 Dec 2026 (standard variable tariff, Direct Debit, England, Scotland & Wales).

About these figures

Source for the typical figure: CSE 'What uses watt?' table. See how we calculate.

Ways to cut the cost

  • Run it on the lowest setting that does the job.
  • Close curtains on the sunny side during the day.
  • Use a timer so it isn't left running in an empty room.

Questions

How much does it cost to run a bathroom extractor fan per hour?

At 26.32p/kWh, a 20W model costs about 0.5p an hour while it's running.

How much does it cost to run a bathroom extractor fan per year?

About £1.92 a year, based on 30 minutes per use, 14 uses a week. Change the sliders above to match how you use yours.

Is the standing charge included?

No. You pay the standing charge every day whether or not the appliance is used, so it isn't part of the cost of running it.

How do I find my bathroom extractor fan's actual power use?

Check the rating label, plug or manual for the wattage, or the energy label for kWh figures. A plug-in energy monitor shows exactly what it uses.
